references.context: Linear algebra: identity K-linear endomorphism I_V:V→V of a K-vector space V, sending each v to itself; no finite-dimensionality assumption.

references.context: Linear algebra: pointwise linear combination of K-linear endomorphisms of V, specifically (A−λI_V)(v)=A(v)−λv for v∈V.

references.disposition: Nontriviality of the already-linked linear kernel is exactly the eigenvalue defining predicate: there exists a nonzero v with (A−λI_V)v=0. No separate kernel notion is needed.
Lambda must belong to the scalar field of V, not an eigenvalue in an unstated field extension.

references.matching_note: The given prime p and its residue classes concern ordinary integers.
The quotient by a prime integer has p elements and forms a finite field.

references.context: Elementary number theory: positive integer p greater than one whose positive divisors are exactly 1 and p; this is an integer prime, not a prime ideal of a ring.
references.reason: The indexed corpus has prime ideals but no corresponding standalone prime integer definition.
references.matching_note: Global candidate-alias audit with the previously recorded prime-integer occurrence required.

references.context: Commutative algebra: quotient ring A/I of a commutative unital ring A by an ideal I, with elements additive cosets a+I, operations induced from A and canonical surjective unital quotient map A→A/I. This includes prime-ideal quotients, polynomial-ring quotients and ideal-power quotients; a quotient's being a field, local ring or R-algebra requires additional conditions.
references.matching_note: This is the ordinary quotient ring by an ideal. Distinct specific features of this occurrence (prime ideal, polynomial base ring, local ring, square-zero ideal or powers) remain in its mathematical source. It is not a general quotient module or a quotient topology.

references.context: Elementary number theory: congruence classes [n] modulo positive integer p, with m equivalent to n when p divides m−n; classes form Z/pZ under inherited operations.
references.reason: This presupposes the integer-congruence relation, not only an arbitrary set quotient or the underlying quotient-ring notation already recorded.
references.matching_note: Audit against modulo-n congruence and Z/(p) quotient-ring references, preserving each mathematical scope.

references.disposition: The quotient inherits the usual addition and multiplication of integer residue classes.

references.matching_note: The coefficient field has characteristic p.
This is the existing field-characteristic notion.
The extension has a Galois automorphism group, with an additional cyclicity condition.

references.context: Group theory: group generated by one element g with g^p=e and no smaller positive period, hence p elements; in this source it is the Galois automorphism group.
references.reason: Cyclic group structure and finite group order are prerequisites beyond merely having a Galois group.
references.matching_note: Compare with Kummer-extension cyclic Galois candidate; do not conflate characteristic and group order.

references.context: Field theory: simple field adjunction K(α) obtained by adjoining a root α of the Artin–Schreier polynomial X^p−X−a over characteristic-p field K.
references.reason: The constructed field K(α) and root-adjunction step are independent prerequisites, not the conclusion that its Galois group is cyclic.
